city_center.name: Baltimore Public Markets (Lexington Market / Cross Street Market) + Inner Harbor
city_center.landmark: Lexington Market (est. 1782), one of the oldest continuously operating public markets in the US; Inner Harbor; Formstone rowhouses with white marble stoops
city_center.notes: Lexington Market is among the oldest continuously running public markets in the country. Baltimore's signature residential fabric is brick and formstone rowhouses with scrubbed white marble stoops. sources: lexingtonmarket.com; en.wikipedia.org Lexington Market; Formstone.

cultural_notes: Lexington Market (1782) is one of the oldest continuously operating public markets in the US and a Baltimore civic food anchor (source: en.wikipedia.org Lexington Market; lexingtonmarket.com)

the scrubbed white marble stoop on a brick or formstone rowhouse is a defining Baltimore image; formstone (a stucco cladding patented locally) covers many rowhouse fronts (source: Formstone, en.wikipedia.org)

Chesapeake foodways center the region; the Eastern Shore supplies produce, honey, and famous blue crab (crab is out of scope for a breakfast tie but frames the food identity) (source: general Chesapeake foodways framing, publicly documented)
Giant, Weis, Safeway, and ShopRite are the metro grocers; Maryland's Best is the state farm-produce program (source: chain regional footprint; Maryland Department of Agriculture Maryland's Best)

design_palette._provenance_note: rowhouse brick red + scrubbed marble stoop + formstone grounded in Baltimore residential architecture (Formstone, en.wikipedia.org). harbor blue-gray from the Chesapeake / Inner Harbor. honey amber from Eastern Shore produce. hex values are perceptual approximations, not sampled -- flag for brand-fit review against fixed brand palette.
